items.title: Make the S262 recovery failure class structurally detectable
items.why: Phase 0 found a real half-closeout: S262 had handoff/log write-back but no closeout brief until recovery, and generated artifacts could drift before the checkpoint. The repo needs a local contract that notices an incomplete latest-session boundary before an agent calls the session green.
items.recipe: Add a session recovery/closeout boundary checker that reads PROJECT_STATUS.currentSession, verifies the matching docs/CLOSEOUT_BRIEF_S<session>_<date>.md and .cache/closeout-brief-<session>.json exist and parse, confirms the latest WORK_LOG/LATEST_HANDOFF mention that session, and emits a concise recovery ledger. Wire its self-test and check into build:check so missing closeout artifacts become a visible gate.
items.premiseEvidence: S262 recovery had to create .cache/closeout-brief-262.json and docs/CLOSEOUT_BRIEF_S262_2026-07-06.md after the prior session was cut off. build:check initially failed on generated drift before the recovery commit.
items.successOutcome: A future cut-off closeout cannot masquerade as complete: the gate prints exactly which latest-session artifact is missing or malformed and build:check includes the contract.

executionLog.note: Implemented in S263; verified by npm run build EXIT 0 and npm run build:check EXIT 0 (181/181).

items.title: Prevent stale startup context-meter truth from overriding live readings
items.why: During S263 start, the live meter said CONTINUE with roughly 997k tokens remaining, while docs/STARTUP_BRIEF.md still carried an older CONSIDER_CLOSEOUT-style context box from the recovered session. That contradiction wastes goal sessions and can trigger premature closeout behavior.
items.recipe: Add a lightweight startup-brief freshness contract that compares the rendered CONTEXT METER block against a fresh scripts/context-meter.mjs --json reading, failing only when the brief says CLOSEOUT/CONSIDER_CLOSEOUT while live says CONTINUE or when the brief is older than the current session lock. Add a self-test fixture for the stale-warning case and wire the check into build:check after smoke-startup-scripts.
items.premiseEvidence: Live start preflight returned CONTINUE for codex-1m with about 997k tokens remaining; the existing STARTUP_BRIEF context block had stale high-usage messaging from S262 closeout state.
items.successOutcome: Startup surfaces cannot preserve stale context-pressure instructions across recovered sessions.

executionLog.note: Implemented in S263; verified by npm run build EXIT 0 and npm run build:check EXIT 0 (181/181).

items.title: Turn play-next redesign from recurring phantom-open into a sample-ready trigger
items.why: The play-next redesign keeps appearing as high-priority work, but the true-viewport epoch has 0 shown / 0 click since 2026-07-02. The useful work is not copy churn; it is a gate that promotes redesign only when the denominator exists and prints the exact reason while waiting.
items.recipe: Add a sample readiness helper for api/funnel-summary.json families with per-family minimums. For play-next, require post-2026-07-02 shown >= 20 before redesign is considered actionable; expose the result as .cache/cta-readiness.json and make generate-genius-list suppress or annotate play-next conversion items while readiness is waiting.
items.premiseEvidence: api/funnel-summary.json reports family play-next counts shown=0, click=0, since=2026-07-02 even though long-window historical play-next:shown is 60.
items.successOutcome: Agents see 'waiting for 20 true-viewport impressions' instead of repeatedly treating a data-gated redesign as open work.

executionLog.note: Implemented in S263; verified by npm run build EXIT 0 and npm run build:check EXIT 0 (181/181).

items.title: Register and grade the Football GM INP mitigation as a field-soak boundary
items.why: S262 shipped a presentation-phase mitigation for the route with 91 slow-interaction samples, but the closeout correctly said it is not a proven win until fresh field data arrives. Existing field verdict tooling focuses on LCP, so INP mitigation can remain narrative-only.
items.recipe: Extend or companion the field-verdict tooling with an INP route-boundary artifact using data/inp-breakdown.json and RUM history where available. Register the S262 Football GM boundary, emit pending/improved/regressed/neutral with sample confidence, and mirror a public-safe summary into api/ so closeout can cite data rather than memory.
items.premiseEvidence: data/inp-breakdown.json shows /games/vaultspark-football-gm/ with 91 samples, p75 duration 640ms, p75 presentation 351ms, dominantPhase presentation; S262 changed that page and needs post-deploy soak.
items.successOutcome: The next RUM refresh can answer whether Football GM INP improved, pending honestly until both sides have enough samples.

executionLog.note: Implemented in S263; verified by npm run build EXIT 0 and npm run build:check EXIT 0 (181/181).

items.title: Make Trusted Types AMBER actionable without reopening already-burned local sinks
items.why: The active-local manifest reports unresolved active local rows = 0, but the live 30-day TT report window still has 329 reports with warm and stale rows. The current state is correct but easy to misread as either 'done' or 'still broken'.
items.recipe: Add a TT readiness artifact that summarizes active/warm/stale counts, unresolved local count, newest lastSeen, and enforce eligibility. Wire the check as advisory/pass unless unresolved active local rows are present; print the next concrete action: wait for soak, refresh R2, or fix a still-present local row.
items.premiseEvidence: .cache/tt-active-local-sinks.json shows activeLocal=1 and activeStillPresent=0; docs/TT_BURNDOWN_2026-07-06.md shows 329 reports, active-3d=1, warm-7d=16, stale-8d+=28.
items.successOutcome: TT enforcement remains honestly gated, while sessions stop re-burning local rows already proven absent.

executionLog.note: Implemented in S263; verified by npm run build EXIT 0 and npm run build:check EXIT 0 (181/181).

items.title: Explain staging yellow with route-level reason codes
items.why: api/staging-health.json is yellow, but the headline does not say whether this is deploy drift, production bot protection, header mismatch, or shell mismatch. That matters because CANON-007 staging should be actionable, not just colored.
items.recipe: Extend check-staging-parity.mjs to include route reasonCodes such as status-mismatch, prod-forbidden, shell-mismatch, header-mismatch, and staging-unreachable. Preserve the yellow status but make the next action obvious in the JSON and generated public status surfaces.
items.premiseEvidence: api/staging-health.json has status yellow: route / prodStatus=403 while stagingStatus=200, and all checked routes have headerParity=false.
items.successOutcome: Staging parity yellow becomes a diagnosis queue rather than a raw warning.
